newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: RTRS - SFE wheat hedges in thin trading.
newsitem.headline: RTRS - SFE wheat hedges in thin trading.

text.p: Australian wheat futures rose in near contracts but fell in more distant contracts in thin trading on the Sydney Futures Exchange (SFE) on Thursday.
A total of 16 futures trades took place, down on Wednesday's 48 trades, while 10 put options also changed hands.
January 1997 recaptured market attention, with the futures contract adding 50 cents to A$168.00 in 13 trades. Ten put options in A$175.00 January 1997 also sold at a A$10.00 premium.
Other futures contracts traded were March 1997, up A$1.50 to A$171.00, and September 1997, down A$2.00 to A$172.00.
Many were looking to hedge in the lower priced market, Matt Kirk of McIntosh Futures Ltd said.
Main interest on Thursday was in put options, especially after Chicago's overnight rally, which was seen as a technical blip, he said.
The rally simply provided better levels to sell or to hedge down with puts, he said.
But market-makers were still more interested in providing offers than trades, he said.
The prospect was still for lower prices, with Chicago December wheat possibly headed for US$4.00 a bushel, he said.
